context: Tripwire 2 again on PR #503, and David's SECOND authorization on this loop -- which the design permits for him and forbids for me. The head pass returned three fail-open findings: the receipt claim was keyed to the PR and deleted by a fresh check (destroying a live claim mid-flight), a request in the same second as the latest pass read as pending 0 at the cap, and an uncommitted extension receipt activated immediately (so a session that died before committing was offered tripwire 1 again). All three let one authorization produce more than one round -- in the module whose entire purpose is to stop that. He was offered: 1 = fix all three and take one more pass, 2 = merge with the three recorded as gaps, 3 = close unmerged and re-cut smaller. He answered "1", with the ramification stated to him that this would be a 7th pass and his second authorization. Fixes are in c677397. WHY grant 2 FOR ONE AUTHORIZATION, stated plainly because the number is larger than his words: the merge-bar head-commit pass of 2026-08-18T21:15Z was delivered while the loop was already at 5 of 5, so it was counted as a round it had no receipt for. `check` therefore reads 6 delivered against an allowance of 6, and a grant of 1 would fund only the pass ALREADY taken, leaving the one he authorized still refused. Grant 2 = the unfunded pass already delivered, plus his one. The alternative -- exempting merge-bar passes from the round count -- was rejected: changing the counting rule mid-loop, in the loop's own favour, is exactly the self-excusing shape this module exists to prevent. Recorded as gap 8 in the PR body.
